reference_sql:
SELECT c.channel_id,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY a.clicks) AS median_clicks
FROM ad_spend_daily a
JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
WHERE a.spend_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-10-31'
GROUP BY c.channel_id
alternatives:
SELECT DISTINCT c.channel_id,
       MEDIAN(a.clicks) OVER (PARTITION BY c.channel_id) AS median_clicks
FROM ad_spend_daily a
JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
WHERE a.spend_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-10-31'

SELECT c.channel_id, quantile_cont(a.clicks, 0.5) AS median_clicks
FROM ad_spend_daily a
JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
WHERE a.spend_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-10-31'
GROUP BY c.channel_id

other_way.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT c.channel_id,
       MEDIAN(a.clicks) OVER (PARTITION BY c.channel_id) AS median_clicks
FROM ad_spend_daily a
JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
WHERE a.spend_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-10-31'
other_way.tradeoff: MEDIAN over a window puts the median on every row, so it needs DISTINCT to give one row per channel.
